payload.body:
CORRECTION to the slice I sent you minutes ago -- my fault, drop two of the four before you spend time on them.

cc came back with a better-informed split than mine and I have taken it. cc owns the whole help surface (lib/help, bin/.devbin/help/*.md, lib/tmpl/help.md, the generated listing and --why) and all of intent/llm/, which includes MODULES.md. So:

DROP: lib/help and intent/llm/MODULES.md. cc has them. If you have already found something in either, send it to me and I will route it to cc rather than have you both write the same file.

KEEP, and this is now your whole slice: lib/config.reference.yaml and lib/infra.reference.yaml, both directions -- every key documented exists in the reader, every key the reader honours is documented. An undocumented key that works is the same defect as a documented key that does not. lib/cmd/infra and all four infra.d children moved in 0.1.6, so infra.reference.yaml is the likelier of the two to have drifted.

The method stands and it is the part that matters: read the reader, then read the yaml. Not the reverse.

My error here is worth naming because it is the one I keep making: I proposed a split from an inventory I had not finished taking. I listed intent/docs/ and the root .md files and never looked at docs/, which is four files and a thousand lines. cc found it. A split proposed from a partial census hands someone a slice that is wrong at the edges, and the person holding it cannot tell.
